task.description: WF-03 Step 1b re-check: independently verify docs/migration/decisions/0018-branch-protection-posture.md against ISS-0441's acceptance criteria.

result.summary:
Two independent judgement checks (items 1 and 2 of dispatch) hold up -- the enforce_admins:false + distinct --admin design genuinely creates mechanical friction rather than relabeling the status quo, and AC3's Step 4 live-verification plan is genuinely sufficient (explicitly distinguishes the static Step 3 check from a real PR-based rejection/success proof and forbids an unquoted 'verified' claim). However, two independent verification failures were found, either of which is FAIL-worthy on its own under this gate's no-partial-credit rule:

(1) AC4 completeness claim is factually false. The design's Consequences section states its grep for 'hard gate'/'structurally impossible'/'Backend gate'/'Frontend gate' across docs/ is 'confirmed as the complete set' and lists exactly four other-hit files (AGENT_SYSTEM.md, WF-02_requirement_implementation.md, HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md, 0014-scripting-plugin-runtime-strategy.md). Independently re-running that exact grep (`grep -rniE "hard gate|structurally impossible|Backend gate|Frontend gate" docs/`) surfaces THREE additional files the design never mentions: docs/agents/workflows/WF-01_requirement_development.md (REQ-VALIDATOR '⛔ HARD GATE', same agent-workflow-sequencing category as the four cited files -- fine on the merits, but omitted), docs/agents/protocols/GIT_SETUP.md (line 64, 'structurally impossible' -- describes a worktree-checkout limitation, unrelated to CI/merge enforcement, fine on the merits but omitted), and docs/anti-patterns.md (five hits, all descriptive incident narration referencing 'Backend gate'/'hard gates', fine on the merits but omitted). On inspection none of these three actually need correction -- so the design's ultimate conclusion (no other file needs changing) is right -- but the design's own explicit, checkable claim that its grep was run and 'confirmed as the complete set' is false: it did not surface or address a majority of the real hits. A governance ADR asserting a specific verification was performed and completed, when it demonstrably was not, is exactly the kind of unsourced/overstated verification claim core-directives.md's 'Never Call a Red Pipeline OK Without a Source' discipline exists to forbid, applied here to a grep-completeness claim instead of a CI-green claim. This is not close-enough -- fix by either rerunning the grep and explicitly listing/addressing all real hits (WF-01, GIT_SETUP.md, anti-patterns.md included), or removing the overstated 'confirmed as the complete set' language and stating plainly which specific files were checked.

(2) Item (d)'s rejection of enforce_admins:true rests on an inaccurate absolute claim. The design states enforce_admins:true would leave 'no override path at all' because 'there is no human to flip enforce_admins off or click merge anyway.' This is not accurate: the same repo-admin identity that runs Step 2's `gh api --method PUT .../branches/main/protection` to configure enforce_admins:false in the first place retains that same API access regardless of the current enforce_admins value -- nothing about enforce_admins:true revokes an admin's ability to call the branch-protection API again and flip it back to false (or delete protection entirely), then merge, then re-apply protection. So a real, if clunkier and more dangerous, override path DOES exist under enforce_admins:true: reconfigure-merge-reconfigure via the same API credentials already in use throughout this record. The design does not acknowledge this path at all, let alone give a reason for preferring the --admin-flag mechanism over it (plausible reasons exist -- a single atomic flagged merge command is safer than a three-step reconfigure dance that risks silently leaving main unprotected if the restore step is missed or the run crashes between steps; the --admin flag is visible per-merge in mergedBy/mergeCommit metadata whereas a protection-toggle-and-restore is not naturally logged the same way -- but the design must make this comparison explicitly rather than asserting a categorically false 'no override path at all'). This was flagged for explicit re-derivation in the dispatch (item 4) and the missed counter-consideration is real, not manufactured.

Neither gap invalidates decision (a)/(b)/(c) or the Step 1-4 command sequences, which are sound and precisely specified. Rework is confined to two passages.

issues.description: The claim 'confirmed as the complete set' for the docs/ grep is false -- independent re-grep of the same four terms surfaces docs/agents/workflows/WF-01_requirement_development.md, docs/agents/protocols/GIT_SETUP.md, and docs/anti-patterns.md, none of which the design's text mentions or addresses.
issues.required_fix: Rerun `grep -rniE "hard gate|structurally impossible|Backend gate|Frontend gate" docs/` yourself, list every real hit, and for each either (a) confirm it is agent-workflow-sequencing / unrelated-topic / historical narration needing no change (as is true for all three missed files here), or (b) add it to the correction list if it actually asserts CI-enforces-merge. Do not restate 'confirmed as the complete set' unless the enumerated file list in the record actually matches the grep's real output.

issues.description: The argument for rejecting enforce_admins:true asserts 'no override path at all,' which is inaccurate: the same admin credentials used in Step 2 to set enforce_admins:false can, at any time, be used again to PUT branch protection with enforce_admins:false (or delete protection), regardless of the current setting -- so an override path exists, just a heavier/riskier one (reconfigure, merge, restore), not a flag-per-merge one.
issues.required_fix: Either (a) acknowledge the reconfigure-merge-reconfigure path explicitly and give a concrete reason enforce_admins:false + --admin is still preferable (e.g. atomicity of a single flagged merge command vs. a multi-step dance that can leave main unprotected if a step is missed or the run crashes mid-sequence; per-merge audit visibility via mergedBy/mergeCommit vs. a protection-toggle that isn't naturally logged per-merge), or (b) otherwise correct the 'no override path at all' language to state precisely what kind of override is being ruled out (a single-command, per-merge one) rather than claiming none exists in any form.
